title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is working out the complex-analytic modular theory of M_{1,1} in Teichmüller style. The previous page identified the Teichmüller group of genus-1 surfaces with SL(2,Z) = Aut^+(H_1). On this page he adds a 'differential rigidification' of an elliptic curve E/C: a basis φ of the tangent space t_E (equivalently of the invariant differentials). This identifies t_E with C, so E = t_E/H_1(E,Z) becomes C/H for a lattice H in C. Pairs (E, φ) therefore correspond bijectively to lattices H in C.

He then takes a double rigidification. The first part is 'strict Torelli': an oriented basis of H_1(E,Z) = H. The second part is the differential rigidification. Together they amount to giving z_1, z_2 in C^* with tau = z_2/z_1 in the upper half plane D^+. Equivalently, (z_1, z_2) is an R-basis of C that is direct for the canonical orientation. The parameter space is the complex manifold PD^+ = {(z_1,z_2) : z_2/z_1 in D^+} (18), the space of oriented lattice bases.

SL(2,Z) acts on the left by g(z_1,z_2) = (d z_1 + c z_2, b z_1 + a z_2) (19). The matrix of this action is M_g = [[d,c],[b,a]] = transpose of tau_inf(g^{-1}), where tau_inf(g^{-1}) is the matrix from the previous page. The map g -> M_g is a homomorphism, so this is a genuine left action. It induces the standard Möbius action tau -> (a tau + b)/(c tau + d) and changes the homology marking while keeping the curve.

The marginal note says that this is the natural action of the modular (Teichmüller) group via an earlier property. The page ends announcing a formula for the universal bi-rigidified family E_{PD^+}. On the next page this is PD^+ x C / Z^2, with Z^2 acting by z -> z + m z_1 + n z_2. There C^* x SL(2,Z) acts, and the quotient of the family minus its zero section is M_{1,1}.

Purpose: to present M_{1,1} as a double quotient of the space of oriented lattice bases by C^* (rescaling of φ) and SL(2,Z) (change of marking). This is the standard lattice-function viewpoint behind modular forms, set within his Teichmüller/fundamental-group framework for the M_{g,ν}.
errors: No mathematical errors. The action (19) is a left action: M_{gh} = M_g M_h, with M_g = (tau_inf(g^{-1}))^T. It induces the usual Möbius action on tau = z_2/z_1.
Minor imprecision: z_1, z_2 in C^* is redundant once tau = z_2/z_1 lies in D^+ is required (only z_1 ≠ 0 is needed to form the ratio).

ideas.what: Elliptic curve with a basis of the tangent space / invariant differential corresponds to a lattice in C
ideas.modern_name: Pairs (E, ω) ↔ lattices; Katz test objects

ideas.what: Space PD^+ of oriented lattice bases with commuting actions of C^* and SL(2,Z), quotient M_{1,1}
ideas.modern_name: Framed lattices; M_{1,1} = SL(2,Z)\H as an orbifold/stack quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Hurwitz); standard in modular forms texts (Serre, Cours d'arithmétique)

ideas.what: Universal family over PD^+ as PD^+ x C / Z^2
ideas.modern_name: Universal elliptic curve over the upper half plane / Teichmüller space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; e.g. Hain, 'Lectures on moduli spaces of elliptic curves'

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but entirely classical setup: lattices, oriented bases and the SL(2,Z) x C^* action presenting M_{1,1}. Its only interest is that it shows Grothendieck framing it via Teichmüller groups in his own notation.
transcription_corrections: Line 9: 'rigidification double Torelli stricte + différentielle' is confirmed by the image ('rigidification double Torelli stricte + différentielle').

The marginal note (bottom left, written diagonally) reads roughly 'c'est donc, via la prop. (13?) [...], l'opération naturelle [...] pb modulaire qui décrit [...]'. The reference number '(18)' in the transcription is doubtful; it could be (13) or another earlier equation number. 'pas trop nette ?' is uncertain.
Equation label: the action formula is (19); the main text continues 'la famille modulaire bi-rigidifiée E_{PD^+} peut s'écrire'.
